questions.q: In the five-part anatomy of an AI workflow, where does the check belong?
options: Only at the very end, after the action has already finished
Around the action: validate the output before, confirm the result after
Only before the model step, to clean up the incoming data
Inside the model step, by asking the AI to review its own answer
questions.explain: The check wraps around the action. You validate the model's output before acting, then confirm the result afterwards, for example that the CRM really accepted the record.

questions.q: Your enquiry workflow should send any deal above a set amount to a different team. How should you build that routing?
options: Add the amount threshold to the prompt so the model picks the route
Add a second AI step whose only job is to read the amount
Ask the model to return the route along with its classification
Use a plain filter or router step on the amount field
questions.explain: Routing on known values should be a deterministic step. AI is the wrong tool for anything a filter or formula can do exactly.

questions.q: Your triage workflow gives very different outputs for similar enquiries from one run to the next. Using the anatomy, what is the most likely fix?
options: Narrow the model step's task, define the output format and add examples
Add filters and de-duplication to the trigger so runs fire only once
Log every run and send failure alerts to a named owner
Add a check that confirms the CRM saved each record
questions.explain: Output that varies wildly between runs usually points to a weak model step. The fix is to narrow the task, define the output format and add examples.
